svg.text: 1.0 - why evals were part of the system
Designed in from day one, not bolted on: objective, repeatable signal about what works and what doesn't.
Measurement over intuition
human review of migrated content is valuable
but doesn't scale - automated evaluation gives
consistent, objective assessment across
thousands of pages, surfacing patterns manual
review would miss
a number per page, not a vibe per spot-check
Decoupled evaluation ★
evals intentionally separate from the migration
flow - quality is reasoned about independently
of how the content was produced, enabling fair
comparison between different migration
approaches
the most mesh-shaped idea in all of 1.0
Continuous improvement
every migration run produces measurable
outcomes; outcomes inform changes to prompts,
models, context allocation, or memory; the
next run measures whether those changes
actually improved quality
the loop that separates iteration from guessing
What the signal was used for
Assess AI models
which LLM fits which migration task
Optimize strategies
memory + prompt configurations, tuned by evidence
Compare migration approaches
AI-driven vs human-led vs hybrid, judged by one rubric
Why it mattered: this feedback loop is what turns a prototype into an enterprise capability - without it, improvements are guesswork; with it, every change is validated by data.
What survived into 2.0: the starred card became an agent - the eval service is decoupled evaluation given its own address, its own store, and a mode badge on every score.
Different approaches can be optimal for different content types, timelines, or quality bars - universal evaluation lets that be a decision, not an assumption.
